title: How to Generate FBR QR Invoices in Pakistan – Step by Step Guide
metaDescription: Generating QR-coded FBR invoices for Pakistani businesses — complete guide for Pakistani businesses. FBR POS compliance, e-invoicing requirements, and step-by-step setup.
content: ## Introduction As a Pakistani business owner, you are likely aware of the importance of complying with the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) regulations. One of the key requirements for businesses in Pakistan is to generate FBR QR invoices for all sales transactions. The FBR QR invoice is a digital invoice that contains a QR code, which can be scanned by customers to verify the authenticity of the invoice. In this blog post, we will provide a step-by-step guide on how to generate FBR QR invoices in Pakistan. We will also discuss the benefits of being compliant, common mistakes businesses make, and how to implement QR invoicing requirements. The FBR has made it mandatory for all businesses to generate QR-coded invoices to reduce tax evasion and increase revenue collection. Non-compliance with this regulation can result in penalties and fines, which can be detrimental to your business. Therefore, it is essential to understand the FBR law and requirements for generating QR invoices. In this post, we will provide a comprehensive guide on how to generate FBR QR invoices, including the technical requirements and benefits of being compliant. ## What the FBR law says The FBR law requires all businesses to generate QR-coded invoices for all sales transactions. According to SRO 1477(I)/2021, all registered persons are required to print a QR code on their invoices, which contains the invoice number, date, and other relevant details. The QR code can be scanned by customers to verify the authenticity of the invoice. The FBR has also specified the format and requirements for the QR code, which must be followed by all businesses. Non-compliance with this regulation can result in penalties and fines, including a fine of up to Rs 500,000 for each non-compliant invoice. Additionally, the FBR can also impose a penalty of up to 10% of the total tax liability for non-compliance. Therefore, it is essential to understand the FBR law and requirements for generating QR invoices to avoid any penalties or fines. The FBR has also specified the requirements for QR invoicing, including the use of a specific QR code format and the inclusion of certain details, such as the invoice number and date. Businesses must ensure that they comply with these requirements to avoid any penalties or fines. In the next section, we will provide a step-by-step guide on how to generate FBR QR invoices. ## Step-by-step compliance guide To generate FBR QR invoices, businesses must follow these steps: 1. **Obtain an FBR registration**: The first step is to obtain an FBR registration, which is required for all businesses in Pakistan. You can register for an FBR account on the FBR website. 2. **Install FBR-approved software**: The next step is to install FBR-approved software, which is required for generating QR-coded invoices. You can choose from a list of approved software providers on the FBR website. 3. **Configure the software**: Once you have installed the software, you need to configure it to generate QR-coded invoices. This includes setting up the invoice format and including the required details, such as the invoice number and date. 4. **Generate QR-coded invoices**: After configuring the software, you can generate QR-coded invoices for all sales transactions. The QR code must be printed on the invoice and must contain the required details. 5. **Verify the QR code**: After generating the QR-coded invoice, you must verify the QR code to ensure that it is working correctly. You can use a QR code scanner to verify the code. 6. **Store the invoices**: Finally, you must store the invoices in a secure location, such as a cloud-based storage system. This will help you to retrieve the invoices in case of an audit or inspection. By following these steps, businesses can generate FBR QR invoices and comply with the FBR regulations. In the next section, we will discuss common mistakes businesses make when generating QR invoices. ## Common mistakes businesses make When generating QR invoices, businesses often make the following mistakes: * **Incorrect QR code format**: One of the most common mistakes is using an incorrect QR code format. The FBR has specified the format and requirements for the QR code, which must be followed by all businesses. * **Missing details**: Another common mistake is missing details, such as the invoice number or date. The QR code must contain all the required details to be valid. * **Incorrect software**: Using incorrect software is another common mistake. Businesses must use FBR-approved software to generate QR-coded invoices. * **Non-compliant invoices**: Finally, businesses often generate non-compliant invoices, which can result in penalties and fines. Businesses must ensure that all invoices are compliant with the FBR regulations. * **Lack of verification**: Some businesses do not verify the QR code, which can result in errors and inaccuracies. Businesses must verify the QR code to ensure that it is working correctly. By avoiding these common mistakes, businesses can generate compliant QR invoices and avoid any penalties or fines. In the next section, we will discuss how FBR IRIS integration works. ## How FBR IRIS integration works FBR IRIS (Integrated Regional Information System) is a web-based system that allows businesses to integrate their accounting systems with the FBR. The IRIS system enables businesses to generate QR-coded invoices and submit tax returns electronically. To integrate with the IRIS system, businesses must use FBR-approved software, which can communicate with the IRIS system. The IRIS system uses a web service to communicate with the FBR-approved software, which enables businesses to generate QR-coded invoices and submit tax returns electronically. The system also provides a secure and reliable way to store and retrieve invoices, which can be accessed by the FBR in case of an audit or inspection. The IRIS system is designed to be user-friendly and easy to use, with a simple and intuitive interface. Businesses can access the IRIS system through a web portal, which provides a range of features and functions, including the ability to generate QR-coded invoices and submit tax returns. ## QR invoicing requirements QR invoicing requirements are specified by the FBR, which includes the use of a specific QR code format and the inclusion of certain details, such as the invoice number and date. The QR code must be printed on the invoice and must contain all the required details to be valid. The FBR has also specified the requirements for the QR code, including the size and resolution of the code. Businesses must ensure that the QR code is clear and legible, and can be scanned easily by customers. In addition to the QR code requirements, businesses must also comply with other FBR regulations, including the requirement to maintain accurate and complete records of all sales transactions. Businesses must also ensure that all invoices are compliant with the FBR regulations, including the use of FBR-approved software and the inclusion of all required details. ## Benefits of being compliant Being compliant with the FBR regulations has several benefits, including: * **Reduced risk of penalties**: Compliant businesses can reduce the risk of penalties and fines, which can be detrimental to their operations. * **Improved efficiency**: Compliant businesses can improve their efficiency and productivity, by using FBR-approved software and streamlining their accounting systems. * **Increased customer trust**: Compliant businesses can increase customer trust, by providing accurate and reliable invoices, which can be verified through the QR code. * **Better record-keeping**: Compliant businesses can maintain accurate and complete records of all sales transactions, which can help them to track their finances and make informed business decisions. By being compliant with the FBR regulations, businesses can avoid penalties and fines, and improve their efficiency and productivity. In the next section, we will answer some frequently asked questions about generating FBR QR invoices. ## Frequently asked questions Here are some frequently asked questions about generating FBR QR invoices: 1. **What is the penalty for non-compliance?**: The penalty for non-compliance is up to Rs 500,000 for each non-compliant invoice, and up to 10% of the total tax liability. 2. **What is the format of the QR code?**: The format of the QR code is specified by the FBR, and must include the invoice number, date, and other required details. 3. **Can I use any software to generate QR-coded invoices?**: No, you must use FBR-approved software to generate QR-coded invoices, which can be found on the FBR website. By answering these frequently asked questions, we hope to provide more information and clarity on generating FBR QR invoices.
